newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, off lows on short covering.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, off lows on short covering.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower but up from their earlier lows on short-covering, intermarket spreading, and spillover support from CBOT corn and soybeans, traders said.
Wheat was driven lower at the midsession after the EU scrapped a tax on daily wheat exports, raising concerns of a resumption of subsidized wheat sales.

"We came off our lows on a 'dead cat bounce.' It's short covering -- we've broken in almost a straight line from $4.80 (per bushel in KCBT Dec wheat)," a trader said. "You also had some people in Chicago unwinding their (intermarket) spreads."
KCBT wheat closed 1/2 to four cents per bushel lower, with Sept down three cents at $4.40. Dec lost 1-1/4 cents to close at $4.35-1/2 per bushel.

CIS was a major presence on the players' sheet, having sold 2.6 million Dec bushels and one million March. Traders said CIS also bull-spread 1.5 million Dec/March at between 5-1/2 and 4-1/2 cents per bushel. Prudential and Man International each sold at least one million Dec bushels.
KCBT estimated Thursday's volume at 37.875 million bushels, lighter than Wednesday's volume of 38.275 million.
